components: a short upper bar turning sharply at its right end
a diagonal down and left to a long middle bar
an open curve that hangs from the bar, rounds the lower left and finishes along the base
strokeOrder: draw the short upper bar from left to right, then without lifting turn sharply and run down and left onto the long middle bar
without lifting, turn back and run right along the whole middle bar
without lifting, double back a little, drop down and left into the open curve, round the lower left and finish along the base to the right
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 0305d file records そ as a single stroke path in this order and direction: the top bar, the zigzag down onto the middle bar, the run right along it, then the open curve; so there are no pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/0305d.svg, hiragana そ (U+305D HIRAGANA LETTER SO), one stroke path kvg:0305d-s1 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores そ as one directed path in writing order: it starts at the left of the short top bar, runs right, turns sharply down and left to the start of the long bar, runs right along it, turns back and drops into the open curve, which rounds the lower left and ends on the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each part of the stroke runs; where the print glyph has no separate ink for the turn back from the bar into the curve, the path doubles back along the bar.

notes: The so of そこ, there near the listener, and それ, that. Some typefaces print the top zigzag apart from the rest; KanjiVG and this book write it as one stroke.
